name: Question 2
worked_solution:
We will use the following identity:

$$
∇\cdot (f\,F)=f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f
$$

First, we compute $∇\cdot F$ and $∇f.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f & =⟨1,0⟩, \\ ∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y{e}^{-x})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-y{e}^{y})=-y{e}^{-x}-{e}^{y}-y{e}^{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (f\,F) & =f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f \\  & =x(-y{e}^{-x}-{e}^{y}-y{e}^{y})+⟨y{e}^{-x},-y{e}^{y}⟩\cdot ⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =-yx{e}^{-x}-x{e}^{y}-yx{e}^{y}+y{e}^{-x} \\  & =y{e}^{-x}-yx{e}^{-x}-x{e}^{y}-yx{e}^{y} \\  & =y(1-x){e}^{-x}-x(1+y){e}^{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Given that F(x,y)=⟨ye−x,−yey⟩ and f(x,y)=x, calculate ∇⋅(fF).

a
y(1−x)e−x−x(1+y)ey
b
(y−x)e−x−(x+y)ey
c
y(2−x)e−x+x(2+y)ey
d
y(y−x)e−x−x(x+y)ey
e
y(1+x)e−x+x(1−y)ey
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the following identity:

∇⋅(fF)=f∇⋅F+F⋅∇f

First, we compute ∇⋅F and ∇f. We get

∇f=⟨1,0⟩,∇⋅F=∂∂x(ye−x)+∂∂y(−yey)=−ye−x−ey−yey.

Therefore, we have ∇⋅(fF)=f∇⋅F+F⋅∇f=x(−ye−x−ey−yey)+⟨ye−x,−yey⟩⋅⟨1,0⟩=−yxe−x−xey−yxey+ye−x=ye−x−yxe−x−xey−yxey=y(1−x)e−x−x(1+y)ey.
